perOption.label: (A) seeing
perOption.reason: Comparative 'less unnerving ... than seeing someone scribbling': the gerund 'seeing' is parallel to the gerund subject 'Recording an interview' (X is less unnerving than Y, both gerund phrases). Well-formed; no alternative parse renders it deviant.

perOption.label: (B) is
perOption.reason: Subject is the singular gerund phrase 'using a recorder'; 'has some disadvantages and is not always the best solution' coordinates two singular finite verbs sharing that subject. Agreement and parallelism both hold.

perOption.label: (C) to develop
perOption.reason: Standard extraposition: expletive 'It' + 'is more efficient' + to-infinitive logical subject ('to develop the technique ... of selective note-taking'). The parenthetical does not disturb the construction. Well-formed.

perOption.label: (D) trying
perOption.reason: Formal proof by exhaustion of parses: 'but' must coordinate like categories. (i) Parallel to extraposed 'to take down' requires '(to) try', not 'trying'. (ii) As a predicate complement of 'It is' the string 'it is ... trying to get into the habit' is not a coherent copular reading and the shared 'sensible' cannot license a gerund conjunct. (iii) As a free participial adjunct it lacks a referential host subject (the matrix subject is expletive 'it'). (iv) As a gerund subject it never meets a finite predicate before the period — 'as the interview proceeds' is only a subordinate clause — leaving a verbless fragment. All parses fail; the required form is imperative 'try' (or 'to try'). Ungrammatical.

perOption.label: (E) much
perOption.reason: 'much' is a licensed degree intensifier of comparatives: 'much easier and quicker to handle'. ('very' would be ungrammatical here; 'much' is the correct choice.) Also 'It' has a felicitous antecedent (the editing habit). Well-formed.
